data.name: Oniris Basket VR
data.detailed_description:
About the game

Immerse yourself in Oniris Basket VR, a game created for HTC Vive in which you can become a professional All Star player and participate in the famous Three-Point Contest. Enjoy playing basketball in the different, surrealistic scenarios and game modes. Have fun, train and compete to improve day by day.

Key features:

Physics and graphics specifically adapted for virtual reality. Play and move around the court with a complete sensation of immersion.

The scenarios boast numerous details to create a unique climate in each of them. If you add the different type of basketballs and interactable objects, each game will become a new experience.

Several different scenarios:
  • “High School” Court
  • “Salvador Dalí Dreams” Court
  • “2050 worker” Court

Various game modes:
  • Training: Free training on the Salvador Dali Dreams court. Challenge yourself by scoring from different distances and positions. Learning and improving your technique for each one of them.
  • Combo mode: You'll have to score the maximum number of consecutive baskets you can. The player’s position will change randomly and this will gradually increase the difficulty.
  • Three-point contest: You will have one minute to score the maximum number of baskets you can. There will be five racks with five balls on each of them. Remember that Drusiball (the multicolor basketball) is worth double. GOOD LUCK!

In constant development

  • Oniris Basket VR continues to develop. These are some of the features that we plan to introduce in the future:
  • Online multiplayer: Challenge your friends in any game mode in the comfort of your own home.
  • Global scores: Reach the top at the Basket VR ranking on its daily, weekly and historic leaderboards.
  • Extreme combo mode: Play combo mode with new features: fireballs, giant hops, hidden secrets...
  • Left and right-handed adapted gameplay.
  • Improved interactions: new tricks and ways of interacting with the ball.
  • Improved physics and graphics: we keep continuously working on the improvement of these characteristics.
  • Multi language support: the game translated to your local language.
  • Many surprises: ;)

We are also opened to receive new ideas and any kind of feedback. If you have any suggestion you can send it to feedbackBasketVR@oniris-studios.com Thank you!

pc_requirements.minimum:
Mínimos:
  • Sistema Operativo *: Windows 7 SP1, Windows 8.1, or Windows 10
  • Processador: Intel® i5-4590 / AMD FX 8350 equivalent or greater
  • Memória: 4 GB de RAM
  • Placa gráfica: NVIDIA GeForce® GTX 970 Ti / AMD Radeon™ R9 290 equivalent or greater
  • Espaço no disco: Requer 464 MB de espaço livre
  • Compatibilidade com R.V.: SteamVR. Room Scale 2m by 1.5m area required

reviews.review:
I've tried all vr games for Vive with basketball on it, moslty had a basket mode among other contents (like Modbox or Nvidia Funhouse). This one could be the simplest among all, from the technical point, it's very basic. Anyway it's fun and extremely cheap at the moment (40% off during launch) so I feel I should upvote this game.

Oniris Basket VR offers three modes, on three courts (any mode with his court). Without real goals or chart or multiplayer, the only mode who could be fun for more than a few minutes is the training, so you can teleport and play as you want. The overall physics isn't very good, the ball bounces in a very unrealistic way and looks awful, but I can say than the shot itself works pretty well, could be the one I prefer at the moment especially from far shots like 3 point area. The video on the page don't make it justice, you can shoot with the proper position over your head and use your legs too. You miss any weight on your hand, obviously, so it's not like the real world... but it's not bad.

What it's really bad is the graphics. I'm not so interested in the grahpics, but the ball itself is the worst I've ever seen. Textures are very, very low resolution. Super low polygon count too. The basket itself miss the net, or has a rigid net (in the indoor court) that is just horrible... way better no net at all than this one. In the training court, you can see a bridge interrupted like the dev stopped to draw the bridge or clipping cut it.

The music instead is extremely good, you've some very decent backing tracks than add value during your training.

The ball, as I said, it's ok in the shot management. It seems so difficult anyway, for any game (not just this one) to use your hands in the proper way. Here when you grab the ball, your controller is inside the ball! What's the meaning of this? The hand should be over the ball, not inside. Other games offers like a magnetic field, so the ball is not on the hand but closer floating in the air, weird as hell and totally immersion breaking. Every games, including this one, lack to support the second hand to grab the ball or to align the shot. In this context, Oniris Basket is better than other games as I said, but still doesn't feel 100% good. Wrist, support hand, grab the ball with both hands, bounce the ball on the ground like the real words: we need those stuff.

This long review seems strange with a positive rating, but as I wrote it's a cheap game and I really want to support basket games for Vive. You can get for free the Nothing But the Net demo, with a way better technical work behind, but this one feels better during shots. Anyway both are far from be perfect, let's hope in some positive challenging among those games.
